Name: Head
Description: Head shell (front-open, 3mm walls), carries bezel, OAK and 7in display
Purpose: Outer shell of the head that holds the touchscreen, the camera and the bezel. Printed because the shape would be costly to machine and is cheap to reprint after a change.
Notes / dimension source: layout SK_Side_Tower head profile; posts bolt up with 2x M5 into the 2020 bores

Name: HeadBezel
Description: Head front bezel with OAK wedge mount and USB-C pass-through
Purpose: Front frame of the head that holds the depth camera and passes its cable through. A separate print, so the camera mount can change without reprinting the whole head.

Name: OAK_Wedge
Description: OAK-D Pro W 5 deg tilt wedge (VESA M4 to OAK, M3 inserts to bezel)
Purpose: Small angled block that tilts the depth camera 5° down so it sees the floor ahead. Changing the tilt only means reprinting this small part.

Name: LidarPedestal
Description: LiDAR pedestal, M4 to deck grid, M2.5 inserts for STL-19P
Purpose: Raises the LiDAR to the right height so its scan clears the body and the tower. Printed so the height can be tuned cheaply.
Notes / dimension source: height = LIDAR_MOUNT_Z - DECK_Z; LiDAR hole positions APPROX (see RV-512)

Name: Bumper
Description: Front soft bumper (TPU): 2 bumper-switch pockets, 2 cliff-sensor windows
Purpose: Soft front bumper that absorbs light knocks and presses the two bump switches. TPU flexes instead of cracking, and it has windows for the front cliff sensors.
Notes / dimension source: globals BODY_W, BUMPER_T/GAP, BUMPER_Z0/Z1, BSW_Y, CLIFF_*

Name: ChargePadHolder
Description: Charging pad holder with dock-detect magnet pocket
Purpose: Holds the two charging contacts and the magnet the dock uses to detect the robot. Keeps the pads at the exact height and spacing of the dock contacts.
Notes / dimension source: pads at CONTACT_Y; magnet d6x3 for the dock reed/Hall switch

Name: CliffSensorMount
Description: VL53L4CD cliff sensor cradle (50 deg), clamps the end skin to the MidCross
Purpose: Holds a cliff sensor at 50° so it watches the floor just ahead of each corner. Without it the robot could not see a stair or ledge in time.
Notes / dimension source: CLIFF_X/Z/ANG; board screws APPROX (2x M2.5 self-tapping, drill with the board as template)

Name: FrontCasterHousing
Description: Front sprung caster housing (2 guide pins + 2 springs)
Purpose: Housing for the sprung front caster, holding its guide pins and springs. The suspension keeps both drive wheels pressed on the floor over uneven ground.
Notes / dimension source: 10mm travel (carriage top 4 -> 14); bolts to front MidCross member; centre hole clears the caster's M8 stud and nut at full travel

Name: FrontCasterCarriage
Description: Front caster sprung carriage plate
Purpose: Plate that carries the front caster and rides up and down on the springs. It lets the caster move 10 mm to follow bumps and door sills.
Notes / dimension source: goBILDA 3621-0001-0001 M8 stud through the centre, M8 nyloc nut on top; guide pins at +-18 (x); Lee Spring LC 032E 05 S springs at +-18 (y) on 7.0 pilots (spring ID 7.52)

Name: RearCasterRiser
Description: Rear rigid caster riser (captive M8 nut for the caster stud)
Purpose: Spacer that sets the rear caster at the right height and holds its nut. A rigid rear caster with a sprung front one keeps the robot steady without rocking.
Notes / dimension source: goBILDA 3621-0001-0001 M8 x 15 stud; M8 nut dropped into the hex pocket from above; bolts to rear MidCross

Name: ComputeTray
Description: Compute tray: Pi 5 + ESP32 expansion board standoffs
Purpose: Holds the Raspberry Pi 5 and the ESP32 board on standoffs in one place. Keeps the main electronics organised and easy to reach for wiring.
Notes / dimension source: COMPUTE_L x COMPUTE_W; Pi 58x49 holes; ESP32 board 4x M4 APPROX

Name: DriverMount
Description: DFR0601 motor driver mount (M3 inserts)
Purpose: Mounts the motor driver board on threaded inserts. Holds it firmly close to the motors so the high current wires stay short.

Name: SkinSide
Description: Side skin panel with wheel notch (used L and R)
Purpose: Side cover panels, one per side, with a cutout for the wheel. They protect the inside of the robot and give it a finished look.

Name: SkinFront
Description: Front skin panel with status light slot
Purpose: Front cover panel with a slot for the status light. Closes the front of the body and lets people see what the robot is doing.

Name: SkinRear
Description: Rear skin panel with battery drawer opening
Purpose: Rear cover panel with the opening for the battery drawer. Closes the back of the body while leaving the battery easy to reach.

Name: DrawerFace
Description: Battery drawer face with pull handle
Purpose: Front of the battery drawer, with a pull handle. Lets anyone swap the battery in seconds without tools.

Name: BumperSwitchBracket
Description: Bumper switch bracket (Omron D2F, slotted M2), M4 to MidCross
Purpose: Holds a bump switch behind the bumper, with slotted holes. The slots let the team set exactly where the switch triggers during assembly.
Notes / dimension source: D2F holes 6.5 apart, M2 x 10 + washer + nut; datasheet lever travel

Name: DeckPlate
Description: Deck plate 2mm 5052 with 20mm M4 interconnect grid
Purpose: Aluminium top plate that closes the chassis and carries the tower, LiDAR and emergency stop. Its regular hole grid lets new modules bolt on without drilling.
Notes / dimension source: globals BODY_L x BODY_W, DECK_T, GRID

Name: FloorPan
Description: Floor pan 1.5mm 5052 (caster sweep holes)
Purpose: Aluminium bottom plate that closes the chassis from below and carries the casters. Stiffens the frame and keeps floor dirt away from the electronics.

Name: BatteryDrawerTray
Description: Battery drawer tray, 1.5mm 5052 U-channel
Purpose: Metal tray that carries the battery and slides out of the back. Keeps the heaviest part low for stability and makes swapping it quick.

Name: DrawerGuide
Description: Drawer guide, 1.5mm 5052 L-angle (used L and R)
Purpose: Rails the battery drawer slides on, one per side. They guide the drawer in straight so its power connector lines up every time.

Name: MotorBracket
Description: Motor bracket, 3mm 5052 L (face plate inside wheel recess)
Purpose: Bracket that bolts each drive motor to the frame, tucked inside the wheel. Aluminium because it carries the robot's weight; checks show it is 3.4 times stronger than needed.
Notes / dimension source: leg rests on bottom side rail; plate fits inside Wasteland d76 recess; inside bend R1.5 (clears gearbox by 1.1mm - confirm R with fabricator)

Name: ChargePad
Description: Charging contact pad, 1mm brass
Purpose: Brass plates that touch the dock contacts to charge the battery. Brass conducts well and resists corrosion.

Name: ChassisFrame_2020
Description: Chassis frame, 2020 aluminium extrusion weldment
Purpose: Main frame of the robot, built from 20 mm aluminium T-slot extrusion. Strong and light, and parts can be bolted anywhere along the slots, so the design is easy to change.

Name: SensorTower_2020
Description: Sensor tower: twin 2020 posts, brace, rear struts
Purpose: Twin posts that lift the head, screen and depth camera above the body. Same extrusion as the chassis, so the head height is easy to adjust.

Name: Gearmotor_37D_70to1_Enc
Description: Pololu 37D 70:1 metal gearmotor 12V with 64 CPR encoder (helical pinion)
Purpose: Drive motor for each wheel, with a gearbox and an encoder that counts wheel turns. The encoder tells the robot how far it has moved, and the motor runs well within its torque limits.
Notes / dimension source: datasheet Pololu_37D_gearmotor_dimensions.pdf p2 (L=24 for 70:1); hole clocking APPROX

Name: SonicHub_1309_6mm
Description: goBILDA 1309 Series Sonic Hub 6mm bore (M4, 16mm square pattern)
Purpose: Hub that connects each motor shaft to its wheel. An off-the-shelf goBILDA part that fits both the shaft and the wheel bolt pattern.
Notes / dimension source: vendor: 8mm thick, 6mm bore, 4xM4 on 16mm square (pattern per goBILDA 3616 drawing); OD 32 APPROX

Name: Wheel_Wasteland_144x52
Description: goBILDA Wasteland Wheel 144mm dia x 52mm wide (14mm bore, 16/32mm square patterns)
Purpose: The two 144 mm drive wheels. Large treaded wheels roll over door sills and rough floors more easily, and the deep hub hides the motor mount.
Notes / dimension source: goBILDA 3616-0014-0144 schematic: d144 x 52, bore d14, holes d4 on 16 and 32 square, web 4 thick at 16 / 32 from the faces; recess d76 measured off the section (APPROX)

Name: Caster_goBILDA_3621
Description: goBILDA swivel caster, M8 x 1.25 male stud (3621-0001-0001)
Purpose: Swivel casters at the front and back that keep the robot balanced on its two drive wheels. A stock goBILDA part that screws straight into the printed mounts.
Notes / dimension source: vendor STEP gobilda.com/content/step_files/3621-0001-0001.zip: wheel d52.6 x 23.1, trail 21.9, hex face to floor 67.0, M8 x 15 stud, hex 13.9 AF

Name: OAK-D-Pro-W
Description: Luxonis OAK-D Pro W (USB), with USB-C plug keep-out
Purpose: Depth camera that lets the robot see obstacles, people and the docking marker. Wide angle with built-in AI processing, which takes work off the Raspberry Pi.
Notes / dimension source: datasheet Luxonis DM9098 sec 9: 97x29.5x22.9, cams 19.5 from bottom, VESA 2xM4 75; VESA height, USB-C and tripod positions APPROX

Name: LiDAR_STL-19P
Description: LDROBOT STL-19P / D500 LiDAR
Purpose: Spinning laser scanner that maps the room and tells the robot where it is. The main navigation sensor; low cost and well supported in ROS.
Notes / dimension source: datasheet LDROBOT STL-19P v1.0 sec 5.1: 54x46.29x35, dome 35.29x12.8, window 7.8 below top, 3x d2.5 holes; hole x-positions APPROX (+-1)

Name: ToF_VL53L4CD_Adafruit5396
Description: Adafruit VL53L4CD time-of-flight sensor, STEMMA QT
Purpose: Small distance sensors, one per corner, that watch the floor. They detect stairs and drops so the robot stops before it falls.
Notes / dimension source: vendor: 25.5x17.7x4.6; mounting holes and connector side APPROX - measure before printing

Name: OAK_Y_Adapter
Description: Luxonis OAK Y-adapter DM6010 (USB-C data + power split), plugs into the OAK
Purpose: Splits the camera cable into a data line and a separate power feed. The camera can draw more power than the Pi's USB port reliably gives.
Notes / dimension source: vendor STEP github.com/luxonis/oak-hardware DM6010_Y-adapter/Mechanical/y-adapter_20211129.stp (25.5 x 12.6 x 18.6); cable keep-outs assume right-angle USB-C plugs

Name: RaspberryPi5_ActiveCooler
Description: Raspberry Pi 5 with active cooler
Purpose: Main computer that runs ROS 2, navigation and the camera software. The active cooler stops it slowing down under constant load.
Notes / dimension source: datasheet RaspberryPi5_mechanical_drawing.pdf: 85x56, holes d2.7 58x49 inset 3.5; component heights APPROX

Name: ESP32_ExpansionBoard38P_DevKit
Description: ESP32-S Expansion Board 38-Pin (header carrier, DC jack) + ESP32-WROOM-32E USB-C dev board
Purpose: Microcontroller that drives the motors and reads the encoders and safety sensors in real time. Keeps time-critical safety tasks off the main computer.
Notes / dimension source: carrier 77x54, 4x M4 (ProtoSupplies); dev board ~28x56, 1.0in row spacing, measured from team photo; hole positions, header and jack placement APPROX

Name: MotorDriver_DFR0601
Description: DFRobot DFR0601 dual-channel 12A DC motor driver
Purpose: Motor driver that turns control signals into power for the two motors. Its 12 A rating leaves wide headroom over what the motors draw.

Name: EStop_ECS-22RE1RM2Q-020Q
Description: Emergency stop, 22 mm big mushroom, push-lock turn-reset, 2 NC, through the deck
Purpose: Red emergency stop button on the deck that cuts motor power when pressed. A required safety feature for a robot that moves around people.
Notes / dimension source: datasheet ECS A31250 p9 (ECS-22RE1RM2Q-XXXQ): mushroom d41.5, 37.5 above the panel, contact unit 35.7 x 50.8, 47.4 behind the panel face, cutout d22.3, panel 1-6 mm; collar / stem split and mass APPROX

Name: TouchDisplay2_7in
Description: Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2, 7in 720x1280
Purpose: 7 inch touchscreen in the head for showing information and taking input from people. The official Pi display, so it works without extra drivers.
Notes / dimension source: vendor 189.32x120.24, active 155x88; thickness 12 and hole pattern APPROX - use the official mechanical drawing before printing the head

Name: Microswitch_D2F-01L-D
Description: Omron D2F-01L-D subminiature switch, hinge lever, 0.1 A 30 VDC gold contacts (bumper)
Purpose: Small switches behind the bumper that tell the robot it has touched something. A last line of defence if the camera and LiDAR miss an obstacle.
Notes / dimension source: vendor STEP (DigiKey model 368442) + datasheet D2F_0318: FP 10 max, OP 6.8+-1.5, OT 0.55 min, OF 0.78 N max, 2 x M2 holes 6.5 apart

Name: Spring_LeeSpring_LC032E05S
Description: Lee Spring LC 032E 05 S compression spring, 302 stainless (front caster, used x2)
Purpose: Springs that push the front caster down onto the floor. They keep the drive wheels in contact over bumps and stay below their load limit at full travel.
Notes / dimension source: leespring.com datasheet: OD 9.14, wire 0.81, free length 19.05, rate 1.751 N/mm, solid 4.7, max load 23.34 N, 5.71 total coils; modelled at installed length

Name: PowerPCB_Envelope
Description: Power/battery/protection PCB in case - RESERVED ENVELOPE (PCB to be designed)
Purpose: Space reserved for the power board that will protect and distribute battery power. The board is still being designed, so the model holds its size and an estimated mass.
Notes / dimension source: globals PCB_L x PCB_W x PCB_H

Name: Battery4S_Envelope
Description: 4S battery pack ENVELOPE with XT60 (pack model TBD)
Purpose: Space reserved for the 4S battery pack that powers the robot. The pack is not chosen yet, so the model uses a placeholder size and a 900 g estimate.
Notes / dimension source: globals BAT_L x BAT_W x BAT_H; XT60 15.8x8.2x16; pack APPROX until chosen

Description: Heat-set insert M2.5 (Pi 5 x4, LiDAR x3)
Purpose: Threaded inserts melted into printed parts for the Pi and LiDAR screws. Screws can be removed and refitted many times without wearing out the plastic.

Description: Heat-set insert M3 (OAK wedge x2, driver x4, charge pads x2)
Purpose: Threaded inserts for the camera wedge, motor driver and charge pads. Screws can be removed and refitted many times without wearing out the plastic.

Description: Heat-set insert M4 (ESP32 board x4, rear caster riser x4)
Purpose: Threaded inserts for the ESP32 board and the rear caster riser. Screws can be removed and refitted many times without wearing out the plastic.

Description: 2020 inside corner bracket + M4 T-nut set (frame joints)
Purpose: Brackets that join the frame extrusions at the corners. Standard T-slot hardware, so the frame can be taken apart and changed.

Description: M4 x 8 SHCS + M4 slot-6 T-nut (pan, deck, skins, guides, brackets, caster blocks)
Purpose: The main screws and slot nuts that fix panels, plates and brackets to the frame. Using one common size keeps assembly simple and spares easy to stock.

Description: M5 x 12 SHCS (head to post bores)
Purpose: Screws that hold the head on top of the tower posts.

Description: M3 x 6 SHCS (gearbox face to motor bracket, 6 per motor)
Purpose: Screws that hold each motor gearbox to its bracket.

Description: M4 x 8 SHCS (wheel to Sonic Hub, 4 per wheel)
Purpose: Screws that fasten each wheel to its hub.

Description: M4 x 10 SHCS (caster plates)
Purpose: Screws that hold the caster plates to the frame.

Description: M4 shoulder bolt 4 x 20 (front caster guide pins)
Purpose: Smooth bolts the front caster carriage slides on. They keep the caster straight while the springs compress.

Description: M2.5 x 6 self-tapping screw (cliff sensor boards, 2 per cradle)
Purpose: Small screws that hold each cliff sensor board in its cradle.

Description: M4 x 12 SHCS + M4 slot-6 T-nut (cliff cradles through the end skins into the MidCross)
Purpose: Screws that fix each cliff sensor cradle through the cover panel to the frame.

Description: M2 x 10 screw + washer + nut (bumper switches to their slotted brackets, 2 each)
Purpose: Screws that hold each bump switch to its slotted bracket, so its position can be adjusted.

Description: M4 x 8 SHCS + M4 slot-6 T-nut (bumper switch brackets through the front skin)
Purpose: Screws that fix the bump switch brackets to the frame.

Description: Bumper float: 2 x shoulder bolt d5, 4 mm travel, + 2 light return springs (guide pins at +-150)
Purpose: Bolts and light springs that let the bumper push back 4 mm when hit and return afterwards. That movement is what presses the bump switches.

Description: Neodymium magnet d6 x 3 (dock detect)
Purpose: Small magnet the dock senses when the robot is in place. Confirms the robot is docked before charging starts.

Description: XT60 panel-mount female + bracket (drawer blind mate) - bracket TBD
Purpose: Panel connector that plugs the battery in automatically when the drawer is pushed home. No loose cable to connect by hand; its bracket is still to be designed.

Description: Cable grommet d25 / d16 (deck ports)
Purpose: Rubber grommets that line the cable holes in the deck. They protect the wires from the sharp metal edges.

Description: Addressable LED strip, ~260 mm (status light slot)
Purpose: Colour LED strip behind the front slot that shows the robot's status. Lets people see at a glance whether it is driving, charging or stopped.

Description: Drawer latch / magnetic catch (validation recommendation)
Purpose: Catch that holds the battery drawer closed. Recommended by the design checks, since nothing else stops the drawer sliding out.
